correctness.rationale: The crown adjacency rule makes the fort condition exactly b-1_{i in B} !=1 for each omitted left i and symmetrically a-1_{j in A} !=1. An exhaustive symbolic case distinction for a,b<=2 proves the only minimal mixed forts are matching-index four-sets; shore triples cover the >=3 cases. Fort hitting gives the zero-forcing polynomial; disjoint triple packing and an explicit size-four fort when n mod 3=2 give floor(2n/3). Uniform fractional weights 1/3 and dual weights on all shore triples prove Z*=2n/3 for all n>=3. Independent verification: Independently generated crown adjacency for n=3,4,5, enumerated minimal forts and forcing subsets. Minimal fort totals 5,14,30 and generating coefficients n=3 {2:6,3:18,4:15,5:6,6:1}; n=4 {4:30,5:48,6:28,7:8,8:1}; n=5 {6:90,7:100,8:45,9:10,10:1}. The all-order LP certificates were algebraically checked. Inspected verify.py; finite enumeration alone is not the proof.
